title: The First Empire
tagline: The world's first conqueror builds an empire from nothing but will.

scenes.text: Mesopotamia, 2334 BCE. The river cities of Sumer have warred for centuries — Ur, Uruk, Lagash, Kish. Until one man, born in obscurity, forges them into something the world has never seen: an empire.

scenes.speaker: Sargon of Akkad
scenes.text: I was a cup-bearer once. Men laughed at the peasant who dared dream of kingship. Now those cities bow to Akkad. Power is not inherited — it is seized by those bold enough to reach for it.

challenge.instruction: The cup-bearer has seized the throne, and the cities of Sumer must learn it. Win the raid: send the target number of your rival's pieces back to the start.
challenge.fact: The Akkadian Empire (c. 2334–2154 BCE) unified diverse Sumerian city-states under a single ruler for the first time in recorded history — a template copied by every empire since.

scenes.text: Legend says Sargon's mother set him adrift in a basket on the Euphrates — an origin story echoed centuries later in tales of Moses. He rose from servant to conqueror through nothing but will and cunning.

challenge.instruction: The legend says Aqqi the water-drawer lifted the baby from the river and raised him as his gardener. Work the sluices and water every field, as the young Sargon once did.
challenge.fact: The Legend of Sargon, written down long after his time, has the king tell how his mother set him on the Euphrates in a basket of rushes sealed with bitumen, and how Aqqi the water-drawer lifted him out and raised him as a gardener.

scenes.speaker: Sargon of Akkad
scenes.text: Write everything. Every grain of barley taxed. Every soldier mustered. Every law decreed. The empire lives and dies by its records — cuneiform pressed into clay, outlasting the men who made it.

challenge.instruction: Sargon has conquered the city-states. Tour Sumer and win the cities over before Lugalzagesi's loyalists turn them back.
challenge.fact: Sargon of Akkad (c. 2334–2279 BCE) built the world's first empire by combining military conquest with cultural assimilation. His daughter Enheduanna, High Priestess of Ur, is history's first named author.

scenes.text: Three thousand years of Mesopotamian civilization would rise and fall in succession. Each empire learned from the last — a chain of innovation in law, astronomy, and mathematics that underpins our world today. And it began with Sargon's ships, riding at anchor by the quay of Akkad.

challenge.instruction: Sargon's empire lived on its trade as well as its armies. Sail his route from the quay of Akkad to Meluhha and come home with a fortune.
challenge.fact: Sargon of Akkad (c. 2334–2279 BCE) created history's first empire, uniting dozens of city-states under one ruler for the first time. His daughter Enheduanna became history's first named author.

scenes.speaker: Sargon I
scenes.text: The lesson is simple. Ashurbanipal stands at Uruk and the Battlefield has begun. Bring me onto the board, put a General at my side, and let us measure Strength against Strength.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 1 · First Duel. Deploy Sargon I to Uruk, add the General, then tap Sargon I and tap Ashurbanipal to attack. Win one attack.
challenge.fact: In a Local Event every card at the location counts: Sargon I brings 10 Strength, the General adds +2 (or +4 beside a Great Person who shares that identity), and the higher total wins the attack. The loser returns to its owner's hand unless Kill mode is on.
